previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain that worsened with eating and was associated with chest pressure and shortness of breath. Evaluation ruled out cardiac ischemia with normal EKGs and negative troponins, and CT angiography showed no pulmonary embolism, aortic syndrome, or mesenteric ischemia. The abdominal pain improved with sucralfate and acid suppression. Black stools were attributed to iron supplementation, and no active bleeding was found. The patient was discharged home with stable symptoms, continuation of cardiac and diabetes medications, new prescriptions for sucralfate and simethicone, and follow-up planned with gastroenterology for further evaluation of chronic abdominal pain.

ACTIVE ISSUES

#LBP - Likely acute on chronic LBP in post-operative course. 
Unclear what made it acutely worse however. Unlikely epidural 
abscess, osteomyelitis or discitis given abscence of fever, 
luekocytosis, or risk factors such as IVDA. Unlikely epidural 
hematoma given no clinical signs of hematoma on exam. Most 
reassuring is although he subjectively endorses some alterations 
in sensation, it appears that most of these are at baseline, and 
his lower extremity strength is ___ throughout. As such, it was 
decided not to obtain any further imaging during his hospital 
course. He was started on a regimen of toradol, acetaminophen 
and gabapentin around the clock with much better control of his 
pain, and increase in his functional activity. Oxycodone was 
provided as needed for breakthrough pain, although this was 
infrequent.

#Constipation - The patient complained of being unable to have a 
bowel movement during his hospital stay. He was given senna, 
docusate and bisacodyl but still was unable to move his bowels. 
He received magnesium citrate and was offered a tap water enema 
but declined. After a second dose of magnesium citrate, the 
patient began to move his bowels. The patient had multiple bowel 
movements overnight on hospital day #3, and on the day of 
discharge he did endorse some abdominal cramping, although his 
exam revealed a noraml abdomen. It was explained to him that 
this was likely due to the decompression of his bowel after the 
laxative use, and that it should improve with time as his bowel 
movements become more regular.

#Diabetes - The patient's at home regimen of insulin was unclear 
at the time of admission, as such the decision was made to 
maintain him with NPH 30 units AM and ___ with S/S with meals. He 
tolerated this well. On discharge he should return to his at 
home regimen and follow up with his primary care physician for 
ongoing management of this issue.

#HTN - The patient was mantained on his home regimen of 
diltiazem and metoprolol with stable BPs.

#Hypothyroid - The patient was mantained on his home regimen of 
levothyroxine.

#GERD - The patient was mantained on his home regimen of with 
PPI and ranitidine
